Here, G2 is the upstream TF, and it is epistatic to its downstream targets. This is because the TF is a master regulator that controls multiple targets. If you knock out the TF, you get the full effect of losing all targets. If you knock out one target, you get a partial effect. The double mutant of TF and one target is the same as TF alone, because TF already removes that target's function. So the TF mutation masks the target mutation. Therefore, the upstream TF is epistatic to the downstream target. This is a known exception to the simple linear pathway rule. In a branching pathway where the upstream gene regulates multiple downstream genes, the upstream gene is epistatic to any single downstream gene. So "G2 is epistatic towards G1" would be consistent with G2 being a TF upstream of G1 (and G3).
